long_biography.plain_text:
Royal Yacht International began with a practical frustration Tommaso Chiabra noticed while running a university concierge service: yacht enquiries were handled slowly by brokerages making little use of digital communication. He and Manuele Thiella responded with a technology-led research and brokerage service for clients and industry partners.

Chiabra also treated social media as part of the operating model, using Instagram to build a client community and solicit feedback. The company expanded from supply work into sales, charter and new-build representation across an international office network. As chairman, he remains involved in transactions and cultivates long-term relationships with shipyards.

uncertainties: No dedicated Forbes profile was found after exact-name, profile-restricted and Royal Yacht International-qualified searches. Forbes' exact interview feature is retained as reporting evidence but is not proposed as a Forbes social link.

The identity is resolved independently of the owner's vessel relationship. The exact name and Royal Yachts employer match current official Royal Yacht International sources, while Forbes, UNICEF, government and industry records converge on the same Italian founder based in Monaco.

Published sources variously date the brokerage's practical creation, rebranding and legal formation to 2011, 2012 or later. The biographies avoid a disputed founding year; the classifications rely on the consistently supported founder role and documented operating history.

Royal Yacht International is the evidenced first major business and supplied earnings that Chiabra says he reinvested in start-ups. No public ownership percentage, brokerage valuation or personal net-worth estimate was found, so the dossier does not call him a billionaire or assign a precise amount.

Shipping & Maritime remains the primary-industry classification at medium confidence because Royal Yacht International is his long-established, current operating platform. Mangusta Capital is a material current investment role, but no reliable evidence ranks his personal economic interest in the newer fund above the brokerage. Beyond Meat is treated as one successful former portfolio investment, not as the basis for a principal-wealth inference.

Broad Self-made is supported by the founder-built brokerage and reinvestment of its earnings. Self-made — independent start is not used because reliable sources do not establish Chiabra's family or original financing well enough to exclude a material advantage; Self-made — advantaged start is likewise unsupported.

Founder is used as the primary wealth relationship because Chiabra created Royal Yacht International and Mangusta Capital and remains chairman or co-founder. His repeated capital allocation is material context and supports the Venture capital tag, but it does not displace the founder relationship to the original wealth-producing platform.

Venture capital is the minimum useful active tag because official and direct sources establish both a formal fund co-founder role and repeated early-stage investment activity over a decade. The assignment does not rest on the single Beyond Meat investment. Shipbroking is omitted because the active tag's commercial-shipping context may not form a coherent click-through cohort with superyacht brokerage, and no owner-level taxonomy candidate is created.

Companies House and UNICEF support April 1986, but no strong source supplied an exact birth day. Direct interviews establish that Chiabra is from and grew up in Genoa, while weaker lifestyle sources call it his birthplace; place of birth and birth day remain unfilled.
A commercial-register-derived profile gives the middle name Camillo, but no second strong source corroborates it. The middle-name field remains blank rather than importing a single lower-tier result.

Monaco residence is proposed at high rather than very-high confidence because Chiabra's current personal LinkedIn location and commercial-register domicile converge with his chairman role at a Monaco-headquartered company, but no reviewed current source supplies a detailed personal residence statement.

The current official RYI site consistently identifies Chiabra as chairman, although some recent transaction pages also call him chief executive. The stable known-for proposal uses Founder and Chairman and leaves the inconsistent executive wording out.

The personal LinkedIn profile is directly linked from Mangusta Capital's official team page. The Instagram handle is self-identified in repeated direct interviews. No verified personal website, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube or TikTok account met the proposal threshold.

The biographies exclude every personal vessel fact, yacht dimensions, listing and sale values, current office or portfolio counts, celebrity associations, follower counts, private family detail, source narration and classification reasoning. They remain complete if every current vessel relationship changes.

The short-long pair was fact-allocated before drafting. Shared anchors are Royal Yacht International and the technology-service gap; the short alone carries Italian identity, Monaco base, profit reinvestment and Mangusta Capital, while the long alone develops the concierge episode, co-founder Manuele Thiella, social-media method, service expansion and shipyard relationships.

Exact-ID inventory preceded the mandatory Forbes-first public-web check. The assigned dossier did not previously exist, so no backup was required. Only this dossier was created, and no live website action was taken.

review.notes: Terminal resolved-person dossier. Current official and independent sources identify Tommaso Chiabra as the Italian founder and chairman of Royal Yacht International and a co-founder of Mangusta Capital. Shipping & Maritime records the original and best-supported current wealth platform, broad Self-made records the founder-built mechanism without inventing his starting position, and Founder distinguishes his principal relationship from later portfolio investing. Venture capital is assigned only because a decade of repeated investing culminated in a formal fund, not because of one portfolio company. Nothing has been compiled or applied.
